# 7-Day Lisbon Budget Trip Plan

A balanced, budget-aware Lisbon itinerary for **2 adults** from **2026-04-10 to 2026-04-16**, built around your targets: **3 museum visits, 2 food-focused experiences, 1 coastal half-day, and 1 live music evening**.
I’m assuming your **€1,800 total** covers lodging, local transit, food, activities, and incidentals, but **not international flights**.

## Trip Budget and Stay Strategy

| Category | Estimated Total | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Accommodation | €700–€900 | 6 nights in a central apartment or guesthouse |
| Food & drinks | €450–€550 | Mix of casual meals, one splurge dinner, snacks |
| Transit | €60–€100 | Metro, tram, ferry, occasional rideshare |
| Activities & museums | €180–€260 | 3 museums + live music + coastal excursion |
| Buffer | €100–€150 | Rainy-day swaps, extras, contingencies |
| **Total** | **€1,490–€1,960** | Targeting the middle keeps you near budget |

### Best neighborhoods to stay in
- **Baixa/Chiado**: best all-around base for first-time visitors, walkable and central.
- **Bairro Alto/Cais do Sodré**: best for nightlife and live music, but can be noisier.
- **Alfama**: scenic and atmospheric, great for old Lisbon, fewer transit hassles.
- **Príncipe Real**: stylish, calm, good cafes, slightly higher prices.
- **Avenida da Liberdade**: practical and well-connected, often better value than it looks.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary

### Day 1: Arrival + Baixa/Chiado Orientation
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- **Morning:** Arrive, check in, and keep the first day light. If you land early, do a slow walk through **Rossio, Rua Augusta, and Praça do Comércio**.
- **Afternoon:** Ride the metro or walk up to **Chiado** for coffee, bookstores, and viewpoints.
- **Food:** Simple welcome dinner in Chiado or Baixa; aim for a **€15–€20 per person** menu.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€110–€160** including lodging share, meals, and transit.
- **Transit tip:** Use the **Viva Viagem** card and top it up for metro/tram travel.

### Day 2: Old Lisbon + Museum 1
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Explore **Alfama** on foot: Sé Cathedral area, narrow lanes, viewpoints, and a relaxed pace.
- **Afternoon:** Visit **Museu do Fado** or **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** for your first museum.
- **Food:** Casual lunch in Alfama; try a daily special and skip tourist-trap spots near the main viewpoints.
- **Evening:** Sunset at a miradouro, then low-key dinner.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€95–€145**.
- **Transit tip:** Alfama is best walked; use tram/metro only to reach the edge of the neighborhood.

### Day 3: Museum 2 + Park Time in the City Center
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- **Morning:** Head to **Museu Calouste Gulbenkian** for a strong second museum choice with a calmer pace.
- **Afternoon:** Relax in **Eduardo VII Park** or browse shops around **Avenida da Liberdade**.
Media: Alt=Afternoon:** Relax in **Eduardo VII Park** or browse shops around **Avenida da Liberdade**, Lisbon, Portugal
- **Food:** Keep lunch simple; save budget for a nicer dinner later in the week.
- **Evening:** Optional wine bar or early night.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€85–€130**.
- **Transit tip:** This is an easy metro day; avoid taxis unless you’re short on time.

### Day 4: Food-Focused Day + Live Music Evening
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/music-note.svg
- **Morning:** Sleep in and do a café breakfast in **Príncipe Real** or **Cais do Sodré**.
- **Afternoon:** Join a **food-focused experience** such as a market tasting, pastry crawl, or small-group food tour.
- **Food:** Make this your first dedicated food experience; prioritize **pastéis de nata, bifanas, cod dishes, and petiscos**.
- **Evening:** Book a **live music night** in **Bairro Alto** or **Cais do Sodré**. Fado is the safest cultural choice if you want something distinctly Lisbon.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€160–€240** including the food experience and music.
- **Transit tip:** For late return, use a rideshare if trams/metro are less convenient after midnight.

### Day 5: Half-Day Coastal Excursion
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- **Morning:** Do your half-day beach/coastal outing to **Cascais** or **Cais do Ginjal/Almada waterfront**.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3c/Beach_near_Lisbon_Portugal%2C_1994..jpg Alt=Morning:** Do your half-day beach/coastal outing to **Cascais** or **Cais do Ginjal/Almada waterfront**, Lisbon, Portugal
  For the easiest budget-friendly choice, **Cascais** is the best fit.
- **Afternoon:** Return to Lisbon for a slower afternoon in **Belém** or back at your hotel.
- **Food:** Light seafood lunch by the coast if prices look reasonable; otherwise eat back in town.
Media: Image=https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/4/4c/Lisbon_%281600%29_detail_1.jpg Alt=Food:** Light seafood lunch by the coast if prices look reasonable; otherwise eat back in town, Lisbon, Portugal
- **Evening:** Free time for resting, laundry, or a neighborhood stroll.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€70–€130**.
- **Transit tip:** Train to Cascais is usually the simplest option; keep an eye on return times.

### Day 6: Museum 3 + Belém Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- **Morning:** Visit your third museum in **Belém** — a good match is the **National Coach Museum** or **MAAT**, depending on your interests.
- **Afternoon:** Walk the riverside, see **Jerónimos Monastery** from outside if you want to keep costs down, and stop for a pastry.
- **Food:** This can be your second food-focused moment if you want a pastry-and-coffee tasting stop in Belém.
- **Evening:** Easy dinner near your base; keep this a lower-spend day.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€110–€170**.
- **Transit tip:** Belém is straightforward by tram/train/bus, but buses can be faster than trams at busy times.

### Day 7: Flexible Rainy-Day Backup or Final Neighborhood Day
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/cloud-rain.svg
- **Morning:** Use this as a flexible final day: revisit a favorite neighborhood, shop for souvenirs, or do a café-and-viewpoint loop.
- **Afternoon:** If weather is poor, switch to the rainy-day plan below.
- **Food:** Easy lunch and a final seafood or tascas-style dinner.
- **Evening:** Pack and prepare for departure.
- **Cost estimate for 2:** **€80–€140**.
- **Transit tip:** Keep one metro or rideshare budget slot open for departure-day flexibility.

## Rainy-Day Backup Plan

If one day turns wet, swap your outdoor-heavy plan for this indoor route:

- **Morning:** Start with **Museu Nacional do Azulejo** or **Calouste Gulbenkian** if you haven’t already done it.
- **Afternoon:** Move to a covered café, bookshop, or shopping arcades around **Chiado/Baixa**.
- **Evening:** Replace the beach/coastal outing with a long dinner and an early live music or Fado night.
- **Best swaps:**
  - Replace **Alfama walking** with **museum + café**
  - Replace **Cascais** with **Belém museums + pastry stop**
  - Replace **park time** with **tram/metro-based neighborhood hopping**

## Transit Tips That Keep Costs Down

- Buy a **Viva Viagem** card and load it with pay-as-you-go credit or day passes if you’ll ride often.
- Lisbon is very walkable, but **hills are real**; use metro/taxis strategically to save energy.
- Use trams for the experience, not as your only transport plan; they can be crowded.
- For late-night returns from live music, a rideshare may be worth the small extra cost.
- Keep museum and excursion days geographically grouped to reduce transit spending.
